title: How the knee-jerk reflex works
examples: Why does your leg kick when the doctor taps your knee?

explain.say: When a doctor taps just below your kneecap, your leg kicks out by itself. This is the knee-jerk reflex, and it shows a shortcut in your nervous system.

explain.say: The tap pulls on the tendon below the kneecap, which suddenly stretches the big thigh muscle. Stretch sensors in that muscle fire a signal along a sensory nerve.

explain.say: The signal goes to the spinal cord, not all the way to the brain. There it connects directly to a motor nerve leading straight back to the same thigh muscle.

explain.say: The thigh muscle contracts and your lower leg kicks, in a few hundredths of a second. The brain gets the news a moment later, which is why you feel the kick after it happens.

faq.q: Why doesn't a reflex need the brain?
faq.a: In the knee-jerk reflex the sensory nerve connects to the motor nerve right inside the spinal cord. Skipping the trip to the brain makes the response very fast.
asks: Tell me about the spinal cord in a reflex

faq.q: What do the stretch sensors in muscles do?
faq.a: Muscles contain stretch sensors called muscle spindles. When a muscle is stretched suddenly, they fire and trigger the muscle to contract, which helps you keep your balance and posture.
asks: Tell me about the thigh muscle stretching

faq.a: A reflex arc is the nerve pathway of a reflex: a sensor, a sensory nerve, a connection in the spinal cord, a motor nerve, and a muscle. It turns a stimulus into a fast, automatic response.

faq.q: Why do doctors test the knee-jerk?
faq.a: It is a simple way to check that the nerves and the part of the spinal cord that run the reflex are working.
asks: Why tap the knee with a hammer?

faq.q: What is the knee-jerk reflex for in daily life?
faq.a: It is part of the stretch reflex that helps you stand upright. If your knee starts to buckle, the stretched thigh muscle contracts automatically to hold you up.
asks: Why do we have a knee reflex?

facts: The knee-jerk reflex involves only two nerve cells: one sensory and one motor.
The knee-jerk is also called the patellar reflex, after the patella, or kneecap.

quiz.say: In the knee-jerk reflex, where does the sensory nerve pass its signal to the motor nerve?
quiz.show: In the knee-jerk reflex, where does the sensory nerve pass its signal to the motor nerve?
quiz.why: The connection is made in the spinal cord, which makes the reflex fast.

wrong.0: The brain only finds out afterwards; it does not make the connection.
wrong.2: The knee holds the tendon and sensors, but nerve connections are in the spinal cord.
